findings.title: Stale-reminder cleanup runs before cancellation and doesn't exclude cancelled reminders
findings.body: The first step in this cron handler deletes every EMAIL WorkflowReminder whose scheduledDate is already in the past, without excluding rows that have `cancelled: true` but have not yet been processed by the subsequent SendGrid-cancel step (e.g. because a prior cron run failed to reach them, see the for-loop issue below). Since this deletion runs before the `remindersToCancel` query/cancel loop, any cancelled reminder whose scheduledDate has already slipped into the past gets silently purged from the DB without ever calling SendGrid's cancel endpoint. If SendGrid has not already sent the email by that point, it will still be sent, reproducing exactly the bug this PR is meant to fix.

findings.title: Single try/catch around the whole cancellation loop aborts remaining cancellations and drops already-queued deletes
findings.body: The for-loop that cancels scheduled SendGrid sends is wrapped in one try/catch for the entire loop instead of per-iteration. If `client.request` throws for one reminder (e.g. an invalid/expired batch id or a transient SendGrid error), the exception propagates out of the loop, so all remaining reminders in `remindersToCancel` for that cron run are never attempted. Additionally, Prisma delete calls are lazy (`PrismaPromise`); the `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` calls queued into `workflowRemindersToDelete` for reminders processed before the failing one are never executed because `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` is skipped when the exception is thrown. The net effect is that successfully-cancelled reminders can remain in the DB forever as `cancelled: true` (getting re-processed, and re-sent to SendGrid's cancel endpoint, on every subsequent run) and reminders after the failing one in the batch are not cancelled at all during that run, increasing the risk that they later fall into the stale-delete bug above and get purged without ever being cancelled.

findings.title: remindersToCancel query is missing a method filter
findings.body: The `remindersToCancel` query only filters by `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate`, without restricting `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL`. This file is specifically the email-reminder cron job and calls SendGrid's `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` cancel endpoint with `reminder.referenceId`, which for SMS reminders would be a Twilio SID rather than a SendGrid batch id. Currently no code path sets `cancelled: true` for SMS reminders, so this is latent rather than actively triggered, but the missing filter makes the handler fragile to future changes in SMS cancellation logic and is inconsistent with the deleteMany query above it which does filter by method.

findings.title: deleteScheduledEmailReminder with immediateDelete=true never removes or marks the WorkflowReminder row
findings.body: When `immediateDelete` is true and a `referenceId` exists, the function calls SendGrid to cancel the scheduled send and then simply returns — it never deletes the WorkflowReminder row nor sets `cancelled: true`. This is inconsistent with `deleteScheduledSMSReminder`, which always deletes the row after cancelling. Callers that pass `immediateDelete=true` (e.g. handleNewBooking.ts when cancelling reminders of the original booking on reschedule, and the workflow/step-deletion flows in workflows.tsx) rely on this to clean up, but for the reschedule flow in handleNewBooking.ts the original booking row is not deleted, so there is no cascading delete to clean up the orphaned WorkflowReminder record. It will linger in the DB (potentially for days, matching the original scheduledDate) until the cron job's stale-date cleanup eventually removes it, rather than being cleaned up immediately.

findings.title: Guaranteed synchronous reminder cleanup replaced with unawaited fire-and-forget calls
findings.body: Previously, cancelling a booking performed a synchronous `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` for every workflow reminder, included in the awaited `prismaPromises` array, guaranteeing DB consistency regardless of whether the remote SendGrid/Twilio cancellation succeeded. The new code only calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` inside a `forEach` without awaiting them, and the handler returns its HTTP response before these promises resolve. In serverless/edge execution environments, the request lifecycle can be torn down right after the response is sent, which can prevent these in-flight `update`/`delete` Prisma calls from completing, leaving WorkflowReminder rows neither marked cancelled nor deleted for a booking that was just cancelled.

findings.title: File header comment not updated to reflect new cancellation responsibility
findings.body: The top-of-file comment still reads "Schedule any workflow reminder that falls within 72 hours for email", but this handler now also performs cleanup of stale reminders and cancellation of scheduled SendGrid sends for cancelled/rescheduled bookings (the core fix of this PR). The comment should be updated so maintainers understand the full, and now more safety-critical, responsibilities of this cron endpoint.

findings.title: No automated tests added for the new cancellation/cron logic
findings.body: This PR introduces a new `cancelled` field, a deferred-cancellation design split across booking handlers and a cron job, and changes to multiple delete/cancel reminder functions, specifically to fix a subtle production bug (reminders still sent after cancellation/reschedule). No unit or integration tests were added to cover the new cancellation flow (e.g. verifying that a cancelled reminder is actually cancelled via SendGrid before its DB row is purged, or that the cron job doesn't delete unprocessed cancelled reminders). Given the bug class being fixed is timing/ordering-sensitive, the lack of tests makes similar regressions (such as the ordering issue noted above) likely to go undetected.

findings.title: Unused Prisma import after refactor
findings.body: `Prisma` is imported from `@prisma/client` (previously used for `PrismaPromise<Prisma.BatchPayload>` typings that were removed in this refactor), but after the change there is no remaining usage of `Prisma.` in this file. Depending on the project's ESLint/TypeScript strictness (`no-unused-vars`), this can fail CI/build linting.
